privacy.ai_training_note: Privacy policy limits use of uploaded content to the requested processing only: 'only use them to perform requested image or video processing' (section 1) and 'We do not use the photos you provide for any reason other than to provide you with the portrait editing functionality' (section 2). These on-domain statements support that customer content is not used for the vendor's own model training. Separately, Terms of Use section 3.8 prohibits customers from using the platform for 'Research/development of artificial intelligence (in particular generation of training data)', which governs customer conduct rather than the vendor's practices. No dedicated AI-training disclosure exists beyond these statements.

flags: A confirmed data breach in February 2024 exposed 41.4 million records (20M unique emails, API keys, salted MD5 hashes, personal data), verified independently by Have I Been Pwned and BleepingComputer.
An earlier confirmed data breach in 2023 exposed 9GB of customer data through an Elasticsearch server left accessible without authentication.
The company provided no formal incident response or acknowledgment of the breaches, and initially denied a breach occurred despite overwhelming evidence.

The company's Trustpilot account is unclaimed (the company has never claimed ownership) with a rating of 1.7/5 stars (June 2026), a reputational signal of customer dissatisfaction rather than a security control finding.
No SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, or GDPR compliance certifications are available, and there is no dedicated trust center or security documentation.
The DPA URL referenced in the Terms of Use (section 9.1: www.cutout.pro/dpa) returns HTTP 404; the company claims to have a DPA but the document is inaccessible.
Passwords were protected with a weak hashing algorithm (MD5 with salt), which experts described as 'relatively easy to crack by modern standards'.
The breach appeared on BreachForums and Telegram, and the attacker claimed ongoing system access at the time of the breach.
Face data processing uses a third-party cloud provider (AWS) and is cached for 24-48 hours; there is no information on the AWS region used or its compliance.

The Terms of Use (section 3.8) explicitly prohibit customers from using the platform for AI research or training data generation, but there is no statement on whether the vendor uses customer data for its own model training.
The privacy policy and terms are available and address basic data handling, but they lack enterprise-grade security documentation and transparency around past incidents.
